motor.definition: Causing or able to cause motion.

sensor.definition: Any device that receives a signal or stimulus (as heat or pressure or light or motion etc.) and responds to it in a distinctive manner.

circuit-board.definition: A rigid, nonconductive panel holds electronic parts in place and links them through metal tracks formed on its surface.

battery-pack.definition: A group of battery cells and related components assembled to store and supply electrical energy.
battery-pack.exampleUsage: The robot's battery pack was disconnected before maintenance.

gear.definition: A toothed wheel that engages another toothed mechanism in order to change the speed or direction of transmitted motion.

wheel.definition: A simple machine consisting of a circular frame with spokes (or a solid disc) that can rotate on a shaft or axle (as in vehicles or other machines).

axle.definition: A shaft on which a wheel rotates.

frame.definition: The supporting shape or structure of a building.

arm.definition: Any projection that is thought to resemble a human arm.

gripper.definition: A mechanical part that grips objects securely so they can be held, moved, or positioned accurately.

camera-module.definition: A compact electronic component containing a camera sensor and related optics or circuitry.
camera-module.exampleUsage: The robot uses a camera module for visual input.

led.definition: Diode such that light emitted at a p-n junction is proportional to the bias current.

wire.definition: The finishing line on a racetrack.

resistor.definition: An electrical device that resists the flow of electrical current.

capacitor.definition: An electrical device characterized by its capacity to store an electric charge.

transistor.definition: A semiconductor device capable of amplification.

diode.definition: A thermionic tube having two electrodes.

microchip.definition: Electronic equipment consisting of a small crystal of a silicon semiconductor fabricated to carry out a number of electronic functions in an integrated circuit.

breadboard.definition: A wooden or plastic board on which dough is kneaded or bread is sliced.

soldering-iron.definition: A handheld tool with a heated tip used to melt and apply solder, a metal alloy that joins electrical parts.

solder.definition: To join or fuse with solder.

multimeter.definition: A portable instrument that tests several features of electricity, including voltage, current, and resistance, in a circuit.

screwdriver-set.definition: A collection of screwdrivers in different sizes or tip types.
screwdriver-set.exampleUsage: The screwdriver set was stored in the tool drawer.

pliers.definition: A hand tool with two handles used for gripping or cutting.

wire-cutter.definition: A hand tool with two sharp edges designed to cut wire.

wire-stripper.definition: A handheld tool that lets electricians strip the protective coating from the exposed end of a cut wire.

hot-glue-gun.definition: An electrically heated tool that melts adhesive sticks; it can cause burns and should be used only with appropriate supervision and safety precautions.
hot-glue-gun.exampleUsage: The hot-glue gun was used only in the supervised workshop.

allen-key.definition: A tool with a six-sided key used to turn certain screws.

wrench.definition: A tool used for turning nuts, bolts, or pipes.

tweezers.definition: A small tool consisting of two pointed arms used for picking up small objects or plucking hairs.

magnifying-glass.definition: A handheld tool uses a curved lens to make nearby details appear larger for close viewing or reading.

helping-hands.definition: A small workbench tool with adjustable clips used to hold components in position during assembly or inspection.
helping-hands.exampleUsage: The helping-hands tool held the wire steady.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.

monitor.definition: Display produced by a device that takes signals and displays them on a television screen or a computer monitor.

keyboard.definition: Device consisting of a set of keys on a piano or organ or typewriter or typesetting machine or computer or the like.

mouse.definition: A hand-operated electronic device that controls the coordinates of a cursor on your computer screen as you move it around on a pad.

code-editor.definition: A specialized software application for writing, viewing, and editing source code, with features that color code elements, align indentation, and support basic text changes.

usb-cable.definition: A cable used to connect devices or transfer power and data.

controller.definition: A mechanism that controls the operation of a machine.

joystick.definition: A manual control consisting of a vertical handle that can move freely in two directions.

humanoid-robot.definition: A robot built with a humanlike body plan, usually featuring a torso, head, two arms, and two legs. Its machinery may remain visible, or synthetic skin may cover the outside.

drone.definition: Stingless male bee in a colony of social bees (especially honeybees) whose sole function is to mate with the queen.

robotic-arm.definition: Describing equipment that uses a robotic arm to handle objects without direct human control.

wheeled-robot.definition: A robot that moves using wheels.
wheeled-robot.exampleUsage: The wheeled robot followed the marked course.

walking-robot.definition: A robot designed to move using articulated legs rather than wheels.
walking-robot.exampleUsage: The walking robot used six mechanical legs.

line-follower.definition: A robot programmed to detect and follow a visible line on a surface.
line-follower.exampleUsage: The line-follower robot stayed on the printed track.

sumo-robot.definition: A small competition robot designed for robot-sumo matches in which machines try to push one another out of a marked ring.
sumo-robot.exampleUsage: The sumo robot was demonstrated in a supervised robotics competition.

underwater-robot.definition: A remotely controlled or autonomous robot designed to operate beneath the water surface.
underwater-robot.exampleUsage: The underwater robot inspected the model pool.

flying-robot.definition: A robot capable of controlled flight, such as a research drone.
flying-robot.exampleUsage: The flying robot was demonstrated in a controlled lab area.

snake-robot.definition: A long articulated robot designed to move with bending motions resembling a snake.
snake-robot.exampleUsage: The snake robot moved through a narrow test passage.

workbench.definition: A strong worktable for a carpenter or mechanic.

storage-bin.definition: A box or container used to organize and store parts or materials.
storage-bin.exampleUsage: Sensors were sorted into labeled storage bins.

pegboard.definition: A board perforated with regularly spaced holes into which pegs can be fitted.

safety-glasses.definition: A label for eyewear made to shield the eyes from hazards, especially in science labs and workshops.

lab-notebook.definition: A ready-made notebook layout for recording an experiment, with sections for its purpose, materials, method, results, and conclusion.

3d-printer.definition: A device that converts digital text or images into printed pages by placing ink or toner on paper.

laser-cutter.definition: A computer-controlled machine that uses a powerful laser to cut or engrave approved materials; it requires trained supervision, enclosure, and safety controls.
laser-cutter.exampleUsage: Only trained staff operate the enclosed laser cutter.

oscilloscope.definition: Electronic equipment that provides visual images of varying electrical quantities.

power-supply.definition: A device that converts energy from a source into the controlled voltage and current an electrical load needs is called a power supply.

testing-mat.definition: A marked surface used to test robot movement, sensors, or navigation in a controlled area.
testing-mat.exampleUsage: The robot completed its trial on the testing mat.

battery.definition: A collection of related things intended for use together.

humanoid.definition: An automaton that resembles a human being.

rover.definition: A person who leads a wandering unsettled life.

chassis.definition: The skeleton of a motor vehicle consisting of a steel frame supported on springs that holds the body and motor.

track.definition: A line or route along which something travels or moves.

code.definition: Instructions written for a computer to follow when running a program.

algorithm.definition: A precise rule (or set of rules) specifying how to solve some problem.

loop.definition: (computer science) a single execution of a set of instructions that are to be repeated.

function.definition: (mathematics) a mathematical relation such that each element of a given set (the domain of the function) is associated with an element of another set (the range of the function).

debug.definition: To locate and correct errors in a computer program code.

compile.definition: To use a computer program to translate source code written in a particular programming language into computer-readable machine code that can be executed.

variable.definition: (used of a device) designed so that a property (as e.g. light) can be varied.

input.definition: A statement that expresses a personal opinion or belief or adds information.
